title: FOMC meeting Oct 26-27, 2027 (no SEP) — decision Wednesday 2027-10-27, 14:00 ET; day one is the October Consumer Confidence print
source: EST: federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, RE-FETCHED DIRECT 2026-09-06 by this session (HTTP 200, 164,831 bytes, page stamp 'Last Update: August 19, 2026') and re-parsed panel by panel rather than inherited from the proposal. The 2027 panel reads verbatim 'January 26-27 | March 16-17* | April 27-28 | June 8-9* | July 27-28 | September 14-15* | October 26-27 | December 7-8*' under the page's own footnote '* Meeting associated with a Summary of Economic Projections' -- October 26-27 carries NO asterisk and therefore NO SEP. Oct 26 2027 is a Tuesday and Oct 27 a Wednesday, consistent with the two-day convention. THE DECISION DATE HAS A SECOND, NON-FED PRIMARY, which no sibling in this family has had: Kalshi's KXFEDDECISION-27OCT event, read direct from the exchange API this session, strikes 2027-10-27T18:00:00Z with contracts closing 17:59:00Z and expected settlement 18:05:00Z (13:59 / 14:00 / 14:05 ET), and its own rules_primary text states verbatim 'If the Federal Reserve does a Hike of >25bps on October 27, 2027, then the market resolves to Yes.' A venue is not a Board primary and promotes nothing, but it is an independent statement of the same date and the same 14:00 ET convention, which fomccalendars.htm does not carry. THE PARSE IS ASSERTION-CHECKED before anything downstream is trusted, using the traps the siblings banked: cutting each year panel at its own footnote block (the 2027 panel's footnote names a January 25-26, 2028 meeting, which a year-scoped parse returns as a phantom ninth 2027 meeting), expanding the cross-month labels in both their spelled and abbreviated forms AND consuming them before the full-month pattern runs, and excluding the entries the Board itself flags -- 2020's March 2 (unscheduled), March 15 (unscheduled) and March 17-18 (cancelled). It returns 167 scheduled meetings, exactly 8 in every year 2007-2027 except 2020's 7, reproducing the sibling assertion exactly. Filed estimate not for want of a primary but because the same page states verbatim 'Each meeting date is tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it' -- the confirming venue is the 2027-09-14/15 meeting, not a better fetch. notes: CANONICAL FILE written by the fomc-2027-10-26 initial-research lane (2026-09-06) after reading the one prior proposal, proposals/fomc-2027-10-26.from-consumer-confidence-2027-10-26.json, which is now inert. The generalisable gap, worth more than the naming call: the <id>.from-<proposer>.json scheme (#1717) solved same-day ADD/ADD collisions completely but does not solve same-day ALIASING, and --validate's competing-proposal warning keys on the id so it is structurally blind to two ids naming one event. A cheap detector is named rather than built by a research lane out of scope -- warn on any two entries of the same kind whose dates are within two days and whose titles share a distinctive token. WHAT THIS RESEARCH ADDS, and both headline findings are corrections. (1) OCTOBER'S 0.594% DECISION-DAY CELL -- the lowest in the monthly table fomc-2027-06-09 published and the number a reader would quote for this meeting -- IS A BIN-SPLIT ARTIFACT. October (n=8) and November (n=11) are not two months; they are ONE meeting slot, the autumn meeting between the September and December SEP meetings, sorted into two bins by which side of a month boundary it happens to fall on. The 19 instances 2007-2025 are one per year with no gaps, and their decision days form an unbroken 16-day cluster running 10-24 to 11-08 with the boundary cutting it near its own median. Pooled, the honest base rate is 0.778% mean / 0.646% median (n=19); the Oct-vs-Nov split carries permutation P = 0.334 and the pooled slot against the other 137 decision days carries P = 0.475. So the October cell is 24% BELOW the slot it belongs to, on a calendar accident. This matters NOW rather than in general because the slot is migrating across the boundary: 2021-11-03, 2022-11-02, 2023-11-01, 2024-11-07, 2025-10-29, 2026-10-28, 2027-10-27 -- three consecutive Octobers, and 2027 the second-earliest autumn decision in 21 years after 2012-10-24. (2) FOMC DAY ONE IS MEASURABLY QUIETER THAN AN ORDINARY SESSION, WHICH NO LEDGER IN THIS FAMILY COULD HAVE FOUND because every other fomc-* entry is decision-keyed. Modern era 2012-2026, Tuesday day-ones (n=113) against non-meeting Tuesdays (n=648): 0.506% vs 0.691% mean absolute S&P move, permutation P = 0.0131 -- significant, and in the QUIET direction. The tail is the sharper statement: 15.9% of day-ones exceed a 1% move against 23.1% of ordinary Tuesdays and 32.8% of decision days, and exactly ONE day-one in 113 exceeded 2% against 4.6% of ordinary Tuesdays. Honest limits: it reverses in the crisis era (2007-2011, n=24, 1.326% vs 1.106%, P = 0.43) and the 2021-2026 sub-sample keeps the sign and magnitude but not significance (0.547% vs 0.706%, P = 0.11). (3) THE VENUE'S 'MALFORMED BOOK' READING IS CORRECTED, not inherited. On the same twelve-ladder snapshot fomc-2027-09-15 read, six mid-quote inversions appear across four ladders -- and ZERO of the six survive requiring the cheaper leg's ASK to sit below the dearer leg's BID. The flag fires on the 27-million-contract 26SEP front book and on the 1,962-contract 27JUN far book alike, so it measures tick granularity and spread width, not book quality. Concretely: 27OCT is ALSO not single-peaked today under the sibling's own criterion (H26 mid 0.145 above H25 mid 0.125) while carrying 3,470 open interest against 27JUN's 1,962, so the sibling's 'the only malformed book of the twelve' clause is false on its own snapshot -- while its CONCLUSION, that depth is neither sufficient nor necessary for well-formedness, gets a third supporting case. corr(log ladder OI, log H26/H25 mid ratio) = -0.871 at n = 12, a fourth independent replication. (4) THE PROPOSAL'S SEP ARITHMETIC IS VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY AND HOLDS: across the calendar page's 2021-2027 panels, SEP meetings' day-one day-of-month spans 7-21 (n=28) and non-SEP spans 1-6 plus 25-31 (n=28) -- a complete separation -- while the last Tuesday of a month falls on the 22nd through the 31st. So a Conference Board print can only ever collide with a non-SEP meeting. The margin is one day (21 vs 22), so it stays falsifiable rather than a theorem. (5) TWO PROPOSALS RIDE ON THIS MEETING, both filed in the same PR: fomc-minutes-2027-11-17, which the seeding proposal explicitly assigned to this lane, and fomc-2027-12-08 -- the year's final meeting and final SEP, absent from this calendar entirely, and the meeting whose date THIS meeting is the confirming venue for.
